data.narrative:
Captura is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Harry Atwater and CX Xiang that has raised $30M+ to date. The relevant comp universe consists of 8 private frontier-energy peers (including Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Enovix) and 1 public comparable (LNZA), though direct same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within a narrow valuation band are unavailable.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable valuation tool here. Using the $30M total capital raised as a proxy for current pre-money value and applying a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression yields an implied valuation of $60M. Peer-median analysis was not applicable given insufficient datapoints meeting narrow filter criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier peers) within the Climate & Energy sector; the 8 available same-sector peers did not yield the minimum 3 comparable observations needed for robust median derivation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $51M (low) to $69M (high), centered on a $60M median. This range reflects a single triangulation method and carries material uncertainty around stage-typical return expectations and the absence of tightly filtered peer validation. Key risk factors include execution risk inherent to early-stage frontier technology and limited public-market pricing signals for this subsector.
